description: Figure 3 presents a comparison of problem distribution based on correctness under two settings—'w/ knowledge' and 'w/o knowledge'—using Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting. The figure is composed of three pie charts, each representing a different difficulty level: 'easy', 'medium', and 'hard'. The 'easy' problem chart shows a large green segment (61.5%) labeled 'N+K+', a smaller yellow segment (34.6%) labeled 'N-K+', and a small red segment (3.9%) labeled 'N+K-'. The 'medium' problem chart displays a large green segment (65.4%) for 'N+K+', a yellow segment (30.8%) for 'N-K+', and a small red segment (3.8%) for 'N+K-'. The 'hard' problem chart shows a large yellow segment (39.6%) for 'N-K+', a green segment (30.6%) for 'N+K+', a red segment (25.1%) for 'N+K-', and a small orange segment (4.7%) for 'N-K-'. A legend on the right side of the figure identifies the four categories: 'N+K+' (green), 'N-K+' (yellow), 'N-K-' (orange), and 'N+K-' (red). The chart visually demonstrates that for easier problems, the primary issue is a lack of knowledge (N-K+), while for harder problems, the main bottleneck shifts to geometric reasoning abilities (N-K-).
